discovery: Theoretical foundations of quantum computing and quantum simulation with trapped ions and ultracold atoms

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Innsbruck, Austria

subfield: Quantum optics / quantum information and quantum many-body physics
motivation: Cirac and Zoller turned atoms controlled by light into a physical platform for quantum information science. Their 1995 proposal for a trapped-ion quantum computer was the first realistic blueprint for entangling quantum gates, and it guided the experiments that today define ion-based quantum processors. With Jaksch and co-workers, Zoller showed in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model and predicted the superfluid-Mott insulator transition. That prediction was confirmed experimentally and opened the field of analogue quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter. Their later proposals for quantum networks, gauge theories, topological phases and Rydberg-based entanglement set the agenda for experiments worldwide. Few theoretical contributions have moved so directly from proposal to decisive experiment, or so thoroughly reshaped atomic physics, condensed-matter physics and quantum technology.
